results.name: object_list_reference_chain_delete
results.evidence: Walks a linked chain (next-pointer at record offset+8, stride 0xc) inside the array whose data buffer is *(array_ptr+0x34), calling datum_delete on each node before advancing; only caller is the header-sweeping FUN_0048b340 which uses it right before deleting the corresponding list header, matching the 'list object reference' node array created in object_lists_initialize.
results.summary: Given a reference-node data array pointer (EAX) and a chain head index (EDX), deletes every node in that singly-linked reference chain via datum_delete.

results.name: object_lists_initialize
results.evidence: Calls FUN_005380d0 (a data-array constructor) with the literal strings "object list header" and a sprintf-built "list object reference", storing the results in DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468, which every other function in this batch reads as the header/reference-node array pair.
results.summary: Creates the two global data arrays (list headers, and reference-list nodes) backing the engine's object-list system.

results.name: object_list_reference_add
results.evidence: Looks up a header record in DAT_0087a464 by a 16-bit list index, allocates a new node via datum_new in DAT_0087a468, stores param_1 as the node's value field (+4), links it in front of the header's existing head index (+8), and increments the header's count field (+6).
results.summary: Pushes a new value (param_1) onto the front of the reference list identified by a list index in EAX, allocating a node from the reference-node data array and bumping the list's element count.

results.name: object_list_reference_get_first
results.evidence: Reads the head-node index (offset+8) out of the header record selected by in_ECX in DAT_0087a464, writes it to *in_EDX, and if valid follows it into DAT_0087a468 to return the node's value field (+4) while overwriting *in_EDX with the node's next-pointer (+8) for continued iteration; returns -1 for an invalid/empty list.
results.summary: Given a list index in ECX and an output iterator pointer in EDX, returns the first value stored in that reference list (or -1 if empty/invalid) and writes the next node index for iteration.

results.name: object_lists_dispose_empty
results.evidence: Iterates every active entry of the header data array (DAT_0087a464) via FUN_004d0630/manual index stepping; whenever a header's count field (+4, short) is zero it frees the header's reference chain with FUN_0048b220 and deletes the header datum itself.
results.summary: Sweeps the object-list header array and deletes (chain and header) any list whose element count has dropped to zero.
